summary.text: Ron Latz is a Democratic state senator who has represented Minnesota Senate District 46 since January 2013 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A lawyer, he chairs the Senate Judiciary and Public Safety Committee.

paragraphs.text: Ron Latz earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Wisconsin in 1985 and a J.D. from Harvard University in 1988.

His 2026 Ballotpedia survey response says he grew up in Golden Valley, attended Hopkins Public Schools, served as an Assistant Attorney General under Hubert Humphrey III, and now practices law in employment and criminal defense cases.
The response also says he served nine years on the St. Louis Park City Council before being elected to the Minnesota House in 2002 and the Senate in 2006.
Latz represented Minnesota House District 44B from 2003 to 2007 and Senate District 44 from 2007 to 2013, and has represented District 46 since 2013.
According to the survey response, he chairs the Senate Judiciary and Public Safety Committee, was chief author of Minnesota's Red Flag Law, and led Senate passage of an assault weapons ban.
The response says he would continue to pursue gun violence prevention measures and work on housing and health care affordability if re-elected.
Ballotpedia says he and his wife, Julia Shimdov, have two children.
